Subject: Post-call recap: PII handling for prompts/outputs + next steps

Hi Alice / Bob — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and next steps so we're aligned on Acme's requirements and what Redwood can commit to today.

Summary of ask from Acme:
- Confirmation of what is persisted when using the Redwood Hosted API vs Dedicated/Private deployments (prompts, model outputs, logs, backups).
- Exact retention windows, where data is physically stored (region), and whether logs contain PII.
- Controls to disable/limit retention and whether you can run without any Redwood-managed copies of prompts/outputs.

What I said on the call (high level):
- Hosted API (default): we retain request/response logs and diagnostic traces for 30 days to support abuse detection, quality monitoring, and debugging. These logs may include prompt text and model outputs if they are part of the request.
- Dedicated: reserved capacity deployments can be configured to minimize or disable retention — logs can be routed to your VPC, and we can turn off persistent request storage; retention and KMS are configurable.
- Private (on-prem/VPC): data does not leave your environment unless you opt into features that require uploads.

Action items / next steps:
1) I'll pull in our security lead (Neha) to provide a written confirmation with the specific hosted retention windows, regional storage locations, and options to disable retention or enable pseudonymization.
2) I'll attach SOC2 and our standard DPA redline for your legal/compliance review.
3) Propose a follow-up call next week (30 min) to walk through any redlines and the Dedicated/private options if you need zero retention.

If that aligns, I'll follow up with Neha's note and the attachments shortly.

Thanks —

Hi Alice (and Bob) — thanks for the questions. I pulled together written confirmations below — happy to jump on a call if you want to walk through any technical details.

Hosted API (default behavior):
- What is persisted: request metadata, request body (prompts), and model outputs are stored in our request logs used for debugging, abuse detection, and quality monitoring.
- Retention: default retention for request/response logs is 30 days. We retain aggregated analytics data (token counts, latency metrics) longer for trending (up to 2 years) but that analytics data does not include raw prompt or output text.
- Backups/snapshots: we do not copy raw request/response logs to long-term immutable backups beyond operational snapshots used for recovery; those snapshots are retained for a maximum of 90 days and are rotated per our backup policy. Raw prompts/outputs are not included in the multi-year analytics dataset.
- Regions: request logs and storage for Hosted API customers are stored in the region(s) specified on your account. By default we provision us-east-1 and us-west-2. If you require single-region residency (e.g., only us-east-1), we can record that in the account configuration/contract.
- Analytics pipelines: analytics and ML training pipelines operate on pseudonymized aggregates; we do not use raw customer prompts/outputs for model training. Any telemetry that might reference prompt length or error classes is aggregated or tokenized to avoid retaining PII.

Dedicated (reserved capacity):
- For Dedicated deployments in a customer VPC, request/response logs can be routed to your logging endpoint and stored under your control. We provide configuration options to disable Redwood-managed persistent storage of raw prompts/outputs.
- KMS/Encryption: Dedicated customers can integrate with customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest; logs persist only per your configured retention policy.

Private / On-prem:
- Data residency: Private deployments keep data within your environment unless you enable a feature that submits data to the Redwood control plane. By default, no Redwood-managed copies are created.

Controls / Minimization options:
- Retention configuration: accounts can request shorter retention or indicate "no retention" for Hosted API under an enterprise agreement; we'll add a contractual clause in the DPA.
- Redaction: customers can enable client-side redaction to remove PII before sending it to Redwood. We can also offer SDK hooks for hashing/pseudonymization of sensitive fields.

Compliance and artifacts:
- SOC2 Type II: attached (SOC2-Type2-Redwood-Inference.pdf).
- DPA: attached a redline copy (DPA_Redwood-Acme_redline_v2.docx). We're open to negotiated retention clauses for Hosted API in the DPA.

Limitations / notes:
- Hosted API default retains raw request/response text for 30 days. If your requirement is zero persistence under any circumstances, Dedicated or Private deployments are the recommended path.
- We do not use customer prompts/outputs to train our public models; any usage for product-level improvements is on pseudonymized aggregates only and subject to contractual agreement.

Next steps I propose:
- Rishi: confirm whether Acme wants us to set account residency to a single US region (us-east-1) and whether you want a short (0-7 day) hosted retention window or to evaluate Dedicated.
- Legal: review the attached DPA redline; we can schedule a call to walk through redline items.

Happy to provide additional logs/policy excerpts if needed.

Regards,
